beats: Hook (line_qc_pitch_investor_no): the pitch "give me billions of dollars and twenty years; I can't guarantee it will work" and nobody signs (her clip 37:43-38:40, her words only; the investor is invented, and nobody speaks her lines). So what do you show them first? Cast for all of QC01 (the six parts cut from her first lecture, Q25-01): the physicist (older, bald with a fluffy fringe, bushy moustache, goggles pushed up, lab coat) and the student (lanky, a tuft of hair, round glasses, striped long-sleeved T-shirt, messenger bag); both invented. No lecturer figure anywhere and never her likeness: her voice and her slides carry her part. For this part: the investor (stout, slicked-back hair, neat beard, three-piece suit, bow tie, watch chain).

Why so big: factoring-scale machines need millions of qubits at 0.1-0.01% gate error (line_qc_pitch_hangar_fridges; give one sourced estimate, e.g. Gidney and Ekeraa 2021, ~20 million noisy qubits; newer estimates are lower).

NISQ (Preskill 2018): dozens to hundreds of noisy qubits, too few for even one well-protected qubit, which takes hundreds (line_qc_pitch_brick_cottage; her answer 54:40-55:40: a distance-15 surface code, "hundreds of qubits" for about 1e-9).

Wave 3, show something first: small noisy chips beat classical machines on random-circuit tasks (a 53-qubit chip, 2019, Arute et al.; she says 2017: correct it), real but not yet useful, which is why she crosses out "practical" (line_qc_pitch_scribble_contest; clip 41:11-41:47). Never tape p11's machine photos; never name the other advantage labs.
Wave 4, task 1: use noisy machines without error correction: variational algorithms, quantum machine learning (reuse line_dials_engineer: set the knobs, check, set them again).
Task 2: error-corrected machines with cheaper codes: fewer bricks per cottage (back to line_qc_pitch_brick_cottage).

Task 3: scale up. Every qubit needs its own lines out of the fridge, and they bring heat (line_qc_pitch_fridge_spaghetti); hence chiplets and distributed machines (line_qc_pitch_linked_fridges; reuse line_cluster_chip_trio).
Honest limit (2024 deck Q24-02 p40): error correction assumes errors do not grow with the qubit count, and bigger chips may lose quality (line_qc_pitch_souffle).
Cover (line_qc_cover_01_04; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the physicist pitches a giant machine at an easel; the investor sits back, arms crossed, chequebook closed.
